title: Internal or tectonic forces and resultant landforms
competency: Describe internal forces and the landforms they create.

keywords.def: A force from inside the earth that makes the ups and downs of the crust: folding, faulting, volcanism, earthquakes.

en.text: Internal forces come from inside the earth. Folding bends rock layers: an anticline bends up, a syncline bends down. Faulting cracks the crust. Land that sinks between two faults makes a rift valley; land pushed up between two faults makes a block mountain.

screens.title: Squeeze a towel
screens.ask: Push the two ends of a towel lying on a table towards each other. What happens in the middle?
screens.after: It wrinkles into folds. Rock layers do the same when the earth squeezes them: that is folding.

root.label: Forces shaping the earth
root.info: Forces from inside build ups and downs; forces from outside wear them down.

children.label: External forces
children.info: Act on the surface from outside.

children.label: Erosion

screens.title: Folding
paras: Internal forces come from inside the earth. They form the ups and downs of the crust.
Folding is the bending of rock layers due to earth movements from one or two sides.
Upward bend: anticline. Downward bend: syncline. All layers bending one way: monocline.

screens.title: Fold mountains
paras: Fold mountains form when compression uplifts and folds the crust.
They are usually made of sedimentary rocks along the edges of continents.

screens.title: Faulting
paras: Movements in the crust sometimes make cracks called faults.
Tension pulls the crust apart: a normal fault. Compression pushes it together: a reverse fault.
Land sinking between two parallel faults forms a rift valley. Land uplifted between them forms a block (horst) mountain.
screens.note: The East African Rift Valley runs 7200 km from Syria to Mozambique. The Ethiopian Rift Valley is part of it, with volcanoes, lakes and hot springs.

en.text: Volcanism pushes magma out to the surface; magma that reaches the surface is lava. Extrusive landforms (volcano, crater, caldera, lava) form on the surface; intrusive ones (batholith, laccolith, dyke, sill) form inside the crust. Volcanoes are active, dormant or extinct, and bring both benefits and dangers.

screens.title: Hot springs
screens.ask: Why do many people visit the hot springs of Sodere and Wondo Genet?
opts: Volcanic heat warms the water underground
screens.after: Heat from magma deep under the Rift Valley warms the water. Hot springs are a benefit of volcanism.

screens.title: Volcanism
paras: Volcanism is the process by which molten rock (magma) is forced out to the surface.
Magma that reaches the surface is called lava. It comes out through a vent or through cracks called fissures.
The hole at the top of the cone is a crater. A very wide crater is a caldera. Mount Zuquala has a crater lake.

screens.title: Figure 1.6: volcanic features
items: A very large mass of magma that collects in the crust.
A mushroom-shaped body of rock, smaller than a batholith.
Magma that hardened in a vertical crack.
A near-horizontal sheet of rock between two rock layers.
Lava spreading on the surface: an extrusive landform.

screens.title: Types and effects
paras: Active volcanoes erupted recently and may erupt again: Erta Ale, Fentale, Dubbi.
Dormant volcanoes have not erupted for a long time but may: Tatali, Dabbahu.
Extinct volcanoes are dead: Ras Dejen, Batu, Zuquala.
table: Hot dangerous gases, ash and lava

en.text: An earthquake is a sudden movement of the crust, usually along faults. It starts at the focus; the point above it on the surface is the epicenter. A seismometer measures it and the Richter scale (0–9) gives its magnitude. Most earthquakes happen on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

screens.title: Earthquakes
paras: Earthquakes are sudden movements in the earth's crust caused by movements deep inside.
Vibrations spread in waves from the centre in all directions.
The starting point is the focus. The point on the surface right above it is the epicenter.
A seismometer measures an earthquake; the Richter scale gives its size.

screens.title: Effects of earthquakes
paras: Loss of life and destruction of property.
The crust moves up, down or sideways. Landslides and deep cracks form.
Cities are destroyed; fires and diseases follow. The sea floor rises or falls.
screens.note: The Ring of Fire (Circum-Pacific Belt) has 75% of volcanoes and 90% of earthquakes.
